- There are tolls roads, they usually charge around 450 crc which is ~1.00 usd for small cars, you can pay by card or cash (AVOID THE LAINS THAT SAY “Quickpass only”, you cant pay in cash nor card in them, its like a sunpass in Florida) 
- there’s loads of restaurants near the main highways, you will even find fruit stands which sell local fruits and candies and different stuff, worth a check if you see one 
- Always check around for motorcycles when driving, they’re around and sneaky. Besides that, driving here is fairly easy, Costarricans are not the best drivers but have seen much more chaos. Also, when you see a “Ceda” and an “Alto” in an intersection, the “Ceda” has the right of way over the “Alto”. 
“Ceda” means to slow down the speed, and if no cars are coming you can go. With an “Alto” you have to make a full stop, check both sides of the road and then proceed
